staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. Although its Git HEAD differs from the metadata vulnerable/fixed commits, the staged tree still contains the vulnerable raw `CBS_data(cbs)` call at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:482`, the 46-entry `kAPIs` table, and the saved ASan line numbers in `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc`.

bug_description.original: The SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list function in its current usage expects a NUL-terminated string, but may receive a non-NUL-terminated string if not handled properly, leading to potential security issues. The function should be provided with a NUL-terminated string, such as by using GetString, to avoid this vulnerability.
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with the exact 1-byte witness `0x2d` (`'-'`). `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` initializes a `CBS` over that byte and then calls `CBS_get_u8(&cbs, &index)`. Inside `CBS_get_u8()`, `cbs_get()` consumes the sole byte, advances `cbs->data` to `buf + 1`, and leaves `cbs->len == 0`; `CBS_get_u8()` then stores `index == 45`. Because `index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs) == 45`, dispatch reaches the final lambda at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:481-482`, which calls `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list(ctx, (const char *)CBS_data(cbs))` directly. That passes the empty remainder's end pointer as a textual `const char *` even though `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list()` expects a NUL-terminated signature-algorithm list. In `parse_sigalgs_list()`, the initial loop `for (const char *p = str; *p; p++)` counts characters until `\0`, but here `str` already equals the first byte past the 1-byte fuzz allocation, so evaluating `*p` is immediately out of bounds. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc:614`. The fix in `patch.diff` changes only the fuzz target: it first extracts a `std::string` with `GetString()` and then passes `sigalgs.c_str()`, restoring the required NUL termination.

source.description: Source. This `CBS_get_u8` statement is the earliest project-side consumption of the fuzz buffer on the vulnerable path: it requests one byte from the `CBS`, creating the byte alias `v` and the empty remainder later exposed through `CBS_data(cbs)`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly one byte `0x2d` (`'-'`, SHA-256 `3973e022e93220f9212c18d0d0c543ae7c309e46640da93a4a0314de999f5112`). When `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` invokes `CBS_get_u8(&cbs, &index)`, this call succeeds on that sole byte, aliases `v` to it, and leaves the remainder empty (`cbs->data == buf + 1`, `cbs->len == 0`) before the later `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list` call reinterprets `CBS_data(cbs)` as a C string.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The loop's first `*p` read expects a NUL-terminated string and instead dereferences the one-past-end pointer passed from the harness.
sink.note: The saved ASan stack is `parse_sigalgs_list -> SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list -> std::__1::function<void (ssl_ctx_st*, cbs_st*)>::operator() -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, matching this sink.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The fuzz target passes the remaining `CBS` bytes directly as a `const char *` without materializing a NUL-terminated string first.
root_cause.note: After step 1 empties the `CBS` remainder and step 2 materializes `index == 45`, the dispatch in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` enters this final lambda. It passes raw `CBS_data(cbs)` as a `const char *` without `GetString()` or any other NUL-terminating copy; with `CBS_len(cbs) == 0`, the argument already equals the end of the 1-byte allocation. The fix replaces this call with `GetString(&sigalgs, cbs)` and `sigalgs.c_str()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Call site for the source step. On the 1-byte witness, this `CBS_get_u8(&cbs, &index)` invocation reaches `CBS_get_u8`/`cbs_get`, consumes `0x2d` into `index`, and leaves the `CBS` cursor empty so later `CBS_data(cbs)` points one byte past the allocation.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness byte is `0x2d`, so `index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs) == 45` and this dispatch reaches the final lambda at lines 481-482 that calls `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list`.

coarse_trace.summary: When the harness asks for the first selector byte, `CBS_get_u8` consumes the lone `0x2d`, stores `index == 45`, and advances the `CBS` remainder to `len == 0`, so `CBS_data(cbs)` now points to the end of the 1-byte buffer.
The `kAPIs[index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs)]` dispatch uses `index == 45` to reach the final lambda, which passes raw `CBS_data(cbs)` directly to `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list`.
BoringSSL interprets that caller-provided pointer as a NUL-terminated signature-algorithm string and forwards it into `parse_sigalgs_list` without any length parameter.
The parser's first loop dereferences `*p` to start scanning for `\0`; because `str` is already one byte past the 1-byte fuzz allocation, ASan reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow read at line 614.

fine_trace.note: This step is reached from the harness call `CBS_get_u8(&cbs, &index)`. On the exact 1-byte witness, `cbs_get(cbs, &v, 1)` succeeds, aliases `v` to the sole byte at `buf`, advances `cbs->data` to `buf + 1`, and decrements `cbs->len` to zero. After this step the remaining `CBS` slice is empty and `CBS_data(cbs)` equals the one-past-end address of the 1-byte fuzz buffer.

With `v` from step 1, `*out = *v` materializes the consumed byte as `index == 0x2d` (`45`). That selector value controls which `kAPIs` lambda executes; the empty remainder from step 1 is preserved in `cbs`.

Because step 2 produced `index == 45`, the `kAPIs[index % OPENSSL_ARRAY_SIZE(kAPIs)]` dispatch reaches this final lambda. It forwards `CBS_data(cbs)` directly as a textual C string without `GetString()` or any other NUL-terminating copy. Since step 1 already left `CBS_len(cbs) == 0`, that argument is the one-past-end pointer of the 1-byte fuzz buffer.

This function receives the caller-supplied pointer as `str`. With no length parameter, `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list()` treats `str` as a NUL-terminated signature-algorithm list and passes it to `parse_sigalgs_list()`.

Sink. The parser immediately evaluates `*p` to start counting the textual list length and `:` separators. Because steps 3 and 4 supplied a one-past-end pointer instead of a NUL-terminated string, this first read is the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `ssl/ssl_privkey.cc:614`.

allocation_context.description: Saved ASan allocation stack: the 1-byte fuzz input buffer was allocated in `ExecuteCallback` immediately before invoking `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: n/a: ASan's allocation context is libFuzzer's 1-byte input buffer; the root cause is the fuzz target passing that buffer's end pointer as a C string.

poc.trigger: The exact staged `poc` is a 1-byte file containing `0x2d` (`'-'`). In the saved vulnerable run it is fed to the staged `ssl_ctx_api` target, consumed by `CBS_get_u8(&cbs, &index)` as `index == 45`, and leaves `CBS_data(cbs)` pointing one byte past the allocation before the `SSL_CTX_set1_sigalgs_list` call.

format.name: raw
format.contract: Exact 1-byte input `0x2d` (`'-'`, SHA-256 `3973e022e93220f9212c18d0d0c543ae7c309e46640da93a4a0314de999f5112`). In the staged harness, that byte is consumed as `index == 45`, selecting the final `kAPIs` lambda at `fuzz/ssl_ctx_api.cc:481-482`. No bytes remain in `cbs`, so the call passes `CBS_data(cbs)` (the one-past-end pointer of the 1-byte buffer) as `str`, and `parse_sigalgs_list` immediately overreads it while scanning for `\0`. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witness and dispatch outcome.
